title: IRAGKR: Iterative retrieval augmented generation with fine-grained knowledge refinement
evidence_summary: Dynamic gate combines attention, entropy and POS signals; four QA datasets and two Llama-2 scales. Reports GPU memory, retrieval frequency/time, component ablation, threshold sensitivity and explicit limitations. No repeated-run/significance analysis was established; implementation detail is substantial but no public code artifact was verified.

title: Multi-objective math problem generation using large language model through an adaptive multi-level retrieval augmentation framework
evidence_summary: Mentor model produces the retrieval decision for multi-objective math-problem generation. Six target LLMs are compared with no-retrieval and full-retrieval baselines. Ablates mentor model/objective retriever/similarity retriever; reports generation time and mentor-model training/inference overhead; includes case/failure analyses and sensitivity to example count/similarity measure. No repeated-run uncertainty or significance test was found. Prompts and training details are supplied, while data are available on request and no public code repository was established.

title: Adaptive retrieval-augmented evidence-fusion for highly heterogeneous temporal entity alignment
evidence_summary: Cross-channel candidate consistency decides whether external evidence retrieval is activated. Evaluated on four TEA/EA benchmarks against 17 baselines. Paired t-tests over three independent runs support HHTEA gains; major modules are ablated. Reports average tokens/time and hardware, and stress-tests fact sparsity, timestamp corruption, LLM backbones and hyperparameters. Public benchmark data and detailed implementation are given, but no public ATEA code artifact was established and the paper states data are available on request.

title: Leveraging contextual confidence for smarter retrieval in large language models
evidence_summary: Semantic entropy routes each query to no, single-step or multi-step retrieval, with compression for long contexts. Evaluated on five single-/multi-hop QA benchmarks with fixed and adaptive baselines. Reports retrieval steps and inference time; targeted ablations compare semantic vs predictive entropy and compression; threshold sensitivity and qualitative failure cases are analyzed. No repeated-run uncertainty/significance analysis or public code release was established, though the implementation is described in detail.

title: Retrieval is NOT always needed: Exploring the timing of retrieval in dynamic retrieval-augmented generation
evidence_summary: Sentence-level confidence routes generation among progression, reflection and retrieval. Tested on three knowledge-intensive QA datasets and multiple white-/black-box models. Reports retrieval counts, runtime and GPU settings, and includes reflection/strategy ablations. No repeated-run statistical analysis was established; the paper states code will be available, so reproducibility is coded partial rather than complete.

title: ACRA: An adaptive chain retrieval architecture for multi-modal knowledge-Augmented visual question answering
evidence_summary: Adaptive multi-hop evidence-chain retrieval uses depth-aware thresholds and beam search. Evaluated on WebQA and MultimodalQA with strong multimodal baselines. Comprehensive component and search-strategy ablations plus parameter analysis are reported. Resource evidence is limited to adaptive search behavior rather than explicit latency/token/compute accounting. No repeated-run statistical analysis or public code artifact was established.

title: MoRE-RAG: Bayesian optimal fusion of multiple retrieval experts for retrieval-augmented generation
evidence_summary: Bayesian fusion adaptively weights multiple retrieval experts and modalities. Evaluated on four BEIR datasets plus industrial corpora. Reports detailed hardware/runtime, key experiments repeated three times, paired t-tests, Wilcoxon tests, Cohen's d and power/CI analyses; extensive formula and component ablations and limitations are provided. No public implementation repository was established, so reproducibility remains partial.

title: SA-RAG: Structured and adaptive retrieval-augmented generation for multi-hop question answering
evidence_summary: A graph-state policy selects retrieval/reasoning/termination actions. Evaluated on five multi-hop/long-form QA benchmarks with broad baselines. Reports token use, latency, GPU memory and reasoning actions; statistical analysis includes 1,000-round paired bootstrap, three seeds and McNemar tests. Controlled noisy-retrieval stress tests and case analyses are reported. No public code artifact was verified.

title: ClauseRoute: Risk-aware clause-guided routing for retrieval-augmented legal reasoning
evidence_summary: Dense/sparse ranking consistency drives risk-aware routing to optional Map–Filter–Reduce processing in legal RAG. Fine-grained component ablation, lost-in-the-middle analysis, threshold sensitivity, latency, token counts and per-query monetary cost are reported. Repeated subsampling/averaging is described but no full uncertainty/significance treatment was established, hence SR=P. Public GitHub code is stated in the paper.

title: Incentivizing Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Inner Adaptive Context Selection
evidence_summary: RAG-Attention dynamically selects document-level KV blocks during autoregressive generation. Evaluated on five datasets spanning single-hop, multi-hop and long-context QA and across Qwen/Llama backbones. A bootstrapped significance test (p<0.05) is reported; time/speedup and A100 hardware are given. Top-n/top-k ablations, distractor/position robustness and human evaluation are included. Implementation details and public base models are provided, but no public InnerRAG source-code artifact was established.

title: Mixture-of-RAG: Integrating Text and Tables with Large Language Models
evidence_summary: MixRAG integrates hierarchical text/table representations, ensemble retrieval/reranking and multi-step reasoning. Reports token/time cost, representation/module ablations, scaling analysis and explicit failure cases across multiple generator models. Dataset, code and prompts are stated as publicly available on GitHub. No repeated-run uncertainty/significance analysis was established.

title: Query-Aware Context Selection for Retrieval-Augmented Generation
evidence_summary: A lightweight classifier predicts query-specific context size k and guides an LLM selector. Evaluated on three multi-hop QA datasets with three generators. Ablations isolate classifier/adaptive selection; Bonferroni-corrected significance testing is reported, and a controlled distractor experiment probes retrieval noise. Resource reporting is partial because retrieval quantity is explicit but latency/token/compute accounting is not comprehensive; no public code artifact was established.

title: ThoraxAgent: An intelligent agent-based decision support system for chest radiography analysis with cross-modal dynamic retrieval
evidence_summary: Confidence-guided reasoning adaptively controls cross-modal retrieval depth in a chest-radiography decision-support pipeline. Evaluated on three public medical datasets with multiple backbones; reports retrieval latency, component ablation, threshold/fusion sensitivity, qualitative cases and deployment limitations. No repeated-run statistical analysis was established. Data are available on request and no public code repository was identified.
